program_name: Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity (unibz markets it as 'International Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity'). No separate Italian title is published on either the UNIUD or the unibz page; UNIUD lists it under its Agraria (Agriculture) area as an inter-university (interateneo) laurea magistrale. [uncertain]
level: master (laurea magistrale, 2 years, 120 ECTS, joint degree - 'rilascio del titolo congiunto')
teaching_language: Entirely English. unibz brochure 'At a Glance' states 'Courses will be taught in English' and the admission information states 'The official teaching language is English.' Note that unibz is a trilingual university (IT/DE/EN), but for this specific master only English is the official teaching language and only English is required for admission (no German/Italian entry requirement).
campus: Bozen-Bolzano (unibz campus) for the whole 1st year and administratively for the entire degree. From the 2nd year the student chooses one of four profile tracks hosted at different institutions: 'Innovation and Authenticity of Wines' at unibz (Bolzano); 'Food Quality Control and Management' at the University of Udine; 'Nutrition Sciences' at the University of Parma; 'Food Chemistry' at University College Cork, Ireland (5 available places). So Udine is only a possible 2nd-year track location, not the base campus.
degree_class: LM-70 (Scienze e tecnologie alimentari / Food Science and Technology). Single class, not interclass. Confirmed identically on both uniud.it and the unibz brochure ('Degree class: LM-70').
admission_type: Restricted access (accesso programmato / 'programmazione locale' on uniud.it) with a capped number of places and a merit ranking list. There is no written entrance exam: selection is done by an Admission Committee purely on academic qualifications when applicants exceed available places. Applications are submitted through the unibz online Application Portal, NOT through UNIUD's system.
access_type_detail: 'Programmazione locale' (locally capped access) per uniud.it. Total 48 places for 2026/27: 40 for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (35 in the Early Bird session + 5 in the Late session) and 8 for non-EU citizens living abroad (Early Bird only). unibz brochure summarises this as 'Places available: 40 EU + 8 non-EU'. Any unfilled Early Bird EU places roll over: 'any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application'. Admission is by ranking list, not first-come-first-served.
academic_requirements: Two routes. (1) A bachelor degree in one of the Italian degree classes L-25 (Agriculture and Forestry), L-26 (Food Sciences), L-38 (Animal Production Sciences and Technologies) or L-GASTR (Sciences, cultures and policies of Gastronomy), or the corresponding class ex D.M. 509/99; OR (2) a previous career covering at least 30 ECTS credits in the listed scientific sectors (SSD), which include MAT/01-09, FIS/01-08, CHIM/01-07, CHIM/10-11, BIO/01-05, BIO/09-11, BIO/13, BIO/18-19, MED/07, MED/42, AGR/01-04, AGR/07, AGR/09, AGR/11-13, AGR/15-19, VET/04, VET/06-07, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/13-17, ING-IND/23, ING-IND/25, ING-IND/34, ING-INF/01, ING-INF/05, SECS-P/13, SECS-S/01-02. In addition applicants must 'possess an adequate knowledge of the basic disciplines of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology'. Foreign degrees must carry at least 180 ECTS and give access to a master programme in the issuing country. Not-yet-graduated applicants may apply but must hold the qualification by the enrolment deadline (conditional/reserved admission). Applicants may enrol in a maximum of two programmes simultaneously provided they are not in the same class and differ in at least two-thirds of their content.
entry_exam_or_test: No entrance exam, no TOLC, no SAT, no interview. Selection is a documents-based ranking by the Admission Committee, triggered only if eligible applicants exceed the available places. The only 'exam' that may be involved is the optional unibz Language Centre English proficiency exam, used as one of the ways to prove the B2 language requirement.
entry_test_name_and_deadline: No admission test and therefore no test deadline or OFA threshold (OFA/additional learning obligations are a bachelor-level Italian mechanism and are not applied here). The applicable scoring rule instead: 'The Admission Committee can assign up to a max. of 95 points' based on the final bachelor grade expressed out of 30 (or the weighted grade average out of 30 for non-graduates), +2 points for graduating with honours (cum laude), +3 points for holding at least a C1 English certificate. 'Minimum score for admission is 55/95 points'. Ties are broken first in favour of applicants who have already graduated, then in favour of the younger applicant (art. 3 L. 127/1997). Optional unibz Language Centre English exam sessions for 2026/27: 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 + 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026) for the Early Bird round; 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026) and 27/07/2026 (registration 10-19/07/2026) for the Late round.
reserved_places_non_eu: 8 places reserved for non-EU citizens living abroad, available only in the Early Bird Application session ('Non-EU citizens (living abroad) - Early Bird Application: 8'). Non-EU citizens who already hold a valid Italian residence permit for work, family, political/humanitarian asylum or religious reasons are treated as EU-equivalent and compete for the 40 EU places instead (a study-purpose permit or tourist visa does not qualify). A non-EU applicant who fails to upload the residence permit in the portal is automatically reclassified as non-EU living abroad. Non-EU applicants living abroad pay a non-refundable application fee of EUR 50 and get only one application window - 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.'
admin_seat_university: Free University of Bozen-Bolzano (unibz) is the administrative seat (sede amministrativa). This is the key exception for this programme: although UNIUD lists it in its own Agraria catalogue, the entire application, ranking, tuition payment and enrolment process runs through unibz. UNIUD's own page states 'Tutte le informazioni relative all'iscrizione sono disponibili sul sito della sede amministrativa della Libera Universita di Bolzano' and links to https://www.unibz.it/it/. Partner universities: Universita degli Studi di Udine and Universita degli Studi di Parma (plus University College Cork, Ireland, as a 2nd-year track partner). Joint degree awarded. Consequently this programme is NOT subject to UNIUD's Elix-Forms / UNIUD international admission calendar, and it does not appear on UNIUD's official 'Degrees taught entirely in English' page.
course_status_flag: Active and recruiting for 2026/27. No 'ad esaurimento' (phasing-out / no new intake) marking on either the UNIUD page or the unibz programme page; unibz publishes a full 2026/27 intake with 48 places, an updated admission-information PDF (last update 24.07.2026) and a 2026/27 brochure.
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 is the entry level required to gain admission - failure to prove it means exclusion from the admission procedure. No Italian or German requirement for admission (unusual for unibz, which is otherwise trilingual). Proof can be given in four ways: (1) English as the main teaching language of the final high school year (recognised as C1; foreign qualifications need a letter from the school if the medium of instruction is not stated on the diploma); (2) a bachelor or master degree taught in English (recognised as C1; again a university letter is needed if the medium of instruction is not stated); (3) a recognised international language certificate from the official unibz list; (4) an English proficiency exam organised by the unibz Language Centre, registered through the application portal in the published registration windows. Indicative B2 thresholds from the official unibz recognised-certificates list: TOEFL iBT 72-94; IELTS (Academic or General) 5.5-6.5 (home edition also accepted); Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, or B2 Business Vantage grade B or C, or C1 Advanced at level B2; MET B2 in all four skills; TOEIC Listening 400+, Reading 385+, Speaking 160+, Writing 150+; Aptis ESOL General/Advanced B2; PEIC B2; telc English B2; Oxford Test of English B2; UNIcert Level II; IGCSE/GCSE English as a second language grade A, B or C. Certificates awarded by an Italian public institution are submitted as a self-declaration; those from a foreign public institution require an uploaded scan of the original. Holding at least C1 gives +3 points in the admission ranking.
english_level_exception: No programme-specific exception. B2 is the standard unibz entry level for this master, the same as for unibz's other English-taught master programmes. Important: UNIUD's own programme-specific English rules (e.g. the B1 exception granted for UNIUD's Management Engineering master, versus B2 elsewhere) do NOT apply here, because admission is governed entirely by unibz. The only level-related differentiator is a bonus, not a requirement: 'Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points.' Additionally, an English-medium high school diploma or an English-taught bachelor/master degree is automatically recognised as C1, which both satisfies B2 and earns the 3-point bonus.
english_cert_validity_years: 5 years, per unibz's own rule - not UNIUD's. The official unibz recognised-certificates document states 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January.' (Italian text: valid from 1 January of the fifth year.) Exception: items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' - such as an English-medium high school diploma, an English-taught university degree, or an International Baccalaureate qualification - 'will have unlimited validity'. The numeric value coincides with UNIUD's general 5-year rule, but the governing source here is unibz's Resolution of the University Council 16/2026.
teaching_language_partial_flag: Fully English. Not a partial-English curriculum and not an English branch of an otherwise Italian programme: unibz states the official teaching language is English and the brochure confirms all courses are taught in English, across all four 2nd-year profile tracks (including the Udine, Parma and Cork tracks). No parallel Italian-language curriculum exists. The only nuance worth flagging to applicants is the mobility structure (1st year in Bolzano, 2nd year possibly at Udine, Parma or Cork), not a language split.
application_deadline_eu: Two sessions for 2026/27, both closing at noon local time. Early Bird Application: 02/03 - 28/04/2026. Late Application (open only to EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment): 28/05 - 20/08/2026. An applicant excluded in the first session may apply again in the second. unibz's Faculty may additionally open extra application sessions in August and September if places remain ('Additional Application Session (only for EU citizens)'), announced separately. These are unibz dates and are completely independent of UNIUD's Elix-Forms admission calendar. Note as of 06/09/2026 both published 2026/27 EU sessions have already closed; 2027/28 dates were not yet published at the time of research. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU citizens living abroad may apply only in the Early Bird window: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 (by noon local time), with a non-refundable EUR 50 application fee. There is no late session for them - 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Ranking list published by 27/05/2026; first tuition instalment to secure the place by 05/06/2026 (noon). Non-EU applicants already holding a qualifying Italian residence permit are treated as EU-equivalent and may use the late session instead.
universitaly_deadline: No fixed Universitaly pre-enrolment date is published by unibz for this programme, and the sequencing differs from the usual Italian pattern: at unibz the Universitaly application comes AFTER admission, not before applying. The official instruction is 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal. The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The non-EU applicants page adds 'After you gain admission, you will receive information on how to apply for a study visa to Italy on Universitaly via email.' The practical window is therefore bounded by the ranking publication (by 27/05/2026) and the enrolment deadline (13/10/2026), but no explicit ministerial cut-off date is stated on unibz pages. Applicants should treat the emailed instructions as the operative deadline. [uncertain]
decision_timeline_days: unibz does not publish a decision time expressed in working days; it publishes fixed ranking-list publication dates instead. Derived from those dates for 2026/27: Early Bird closes 28/04/2026 and ranking lists are published 'by 27/05/2026' - about 29 calendar days, roughly 20-21 working days. Late Application closes 20/08/2026 and ranking lists are published 'by 03/09/2026' - about 14 calendar days, roughly 10 working days. Ranking lists are published at https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/ranking-lists and 'are only valid for the respective academic year'. [uncertain]
enrolment_window: Early Bird: pay the 1st tuition instalment by 05/06/2026 (noon) to secure the place, then enrol online in the application portal from 10/07/2026 until 13/10/2026 (noon). Late Application: pay the 1st instalment by 11/09/2026 (noon), enrol from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 (noon). Missing the fee deadline or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant on the ranking list. unibz recommends enrolling as early as possible so that incomplete documents can still be corrected before the deadline. Places are allocated by ranking position, not chronologically, but the seat is forfeited on any missed deadline. Late enrolment fallback: an applicant who obtains the bachelor qualification only after the enrolment deadline 'will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there are study places still available, can enrol by 11 December 2026'. Paying fees does not by itself confer student status - only enrolment does, and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol (the sole exception being non-EU applicants abroad who fail to obtain the necessary documents from the Italian authorities).
required_documents: At application, in the unibz Application Portal: (1) account registration plus a valid ID card or passport, front and back - an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document causes exclusion; (2) qualification evidence - if graduated in Italy, a diploma supplement or a self-declaration under D.P.R. 445/2000 stating the degree awarded with final grade and passed exams, or, if not yet graduated, a certificate listing the exams passed; if graduated abroad, a diploma supplement or final degree certificate with passed exams, or a transcript of records if not yet graduated, in Italian, German or English. These must show the final grade, each passed exam with grade and date, credit points, and (for Italian titles) scientific fields; for foreign qualifications also the grading scale of the issuing university, including the minimum passing and maximum achievable final grade. The Faculty may additionally request course content descriptions or teaching hours; (3) the Excel file template available in the application portal, summarising academic records; (4) English language certification of at least B2; (5) for applicants with a qualification obtained abroad, the diploma of the qualification (uploadable at enrolment if not yet issued); (6) for non-EU citizens claiming EU-equivalent treatment, a copy of the valid Italian residence permit (or a renewal request if expired). At enrolment, holders of a foreign university degree must additionally upload: the bachelor degree diploma; an official translation into Italian (not required if issued in German or English); a diploma supplement showing at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme; and, depending on the education system - (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein: a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database - Italy); (b) non-EU Lisbon Convention signatories: a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI plus a Statement of Verification from CIMEA; (c) non-EU non-signatories: a Statement of Comparability plus a Statement of Verification, both from CIMEA. unibz reserves the right to request further documents and may exclude a student by Rector's decree even after enrolment if the admission qualification proves invalid. Non-EU students who enter Italy must apply for the residence permit within 8 working days of arrival and then hand it in at the Student Office. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ - the unibz (administrative seat) fee page, which is the governing one for this programme; UNIUD's fee pages do not apply. Amounts for 2026/27: approximately EUR 1,200 per year, in two instalments of EUR 600 (the first includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp, due by 13/10/2026; the second due by 31/03/2027). Late payment incurs a EUR 30 fine and blocks the online account. Students two or more years beyond the normal programme length pay a EUR 300 surcharge (first instalment EUR 900). Full exemption (only the EUR 16 stamp) for students with a disability recognised under art. 3 para. 1 of Law 104/1992 or invalidity of 66% or more, and for foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Holders of an Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano scholarship are refunded the fees paid. No refund on withdrawal, interruption or exclusion.
official_program_url: https://www.unibz.it/en/faculties/agricultural-environmental-food-sciences/master-food-sciences-innovation-authenticity - the authoritative page (administrative seat, carries the live admission information). Secondary/partner listing at UNIUD: https://www.uniud.it/it/didattica/corsi/area-scientifica/agraria/laurea-magistrale/food-sciences-innovation-authenticity/corso/food-sciences-innovation-authenticity (descriptive only; it explicitly redirects enrolment questions to unibz).

uncertainty_notes: INTERATENEO EXCEPTION - the central caveat for this record. This is a joint (interateneo) LM-70 degree of UNIUD + University of Parma + Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, administratively seated at unibz. UNIUD lists it in its Agraria course catalogue but it is deliberately absent from UNIUD's official 'Degrees taught entirely in English' page, because no part of the admission process runs through UNIUD. Every process field in this record (admission type and scoring, places, deadlines, language proof, required documents, fees, enrolment) is sourced from unibz, not uniud.it; uniud.it was used only for the degree class, the joint-degree/local-programming status, the partner list and the pointer to unibz. Specific consequences: (a) UNIUD's Elix-Forms application platform and UNIUD's international admission calendar do NOT apply - applications go through the unibz Application Portal; (b) UNIUD's programme-specific English rules (such as the B1 exception for Management Engineering) do not apply - unibz's flat B2 rule governs; (c) the 5-year certificate validity happens to match UNIUD's general rule but derives from unibz's own Resolution 16/2026, so it could diverge in future years; (d) UNIUD's fee/ISEE scheme does not apply - unibz's flat approx. EUR 1,200/year applies, with no ISEE-based banding for this programme. TIMING CAVEAT: research was carried out on 06/09/2026 and all dates above are the published 2026/27 cycle. Both 2026/27 EU application sessions (closed 28/04/2026 and 20/08/2026) and the non-EU session had already closed by the research date; only the enrolment window (to 13/10/2026) and possible unibz-announced additional EU-only sessions remained open. 2027/28 dates had not been published; unibz's admission information PDF is explicitly marked 'Subject to change.' with 'Latest update: 24.07.2026', so 2027/28 deadlines must be re-verified when unibz republishes. UNIVERSITALY: unibz publishes no fixed Universitaly pre-enrolment cut-off for this programme and inverts the usual Italian order - Universitaly is completed after admission and after paying the first instalment, with instructions sent by email, not before applying. The window is therefore only inferable (ranking publication by 27/05/2026 through enrolment by 13/10/2026) and is marked uncertain; the Italian ministry's own general 2026/27 pre-enrolment cut-offs reported by third-party sources were not confirmed on any unibz or MUR page and were not used. DECISION TIMELINE: unibz never expresses a decision time in working days; the figures given are calculated from published ranking-publication dates and are therefore derived, not quoted. PLACE COUNTS: a third-party aggregator reported '30 EU + 5 non-EU' for an earlier cycle; the current official 2026/27 figure is 40 EU (35 Early Bird + 5 Late) + 8 non-EU, taken from the unibz brochure and admission-information PDF. The aggregator figure was discarded. PROGRAMME NAME: no official Italian-language title is published on either site, so only the English title is recorded. CAMPUS: recorded as Bolzano because the first year and the administrative seat are there; a student who selects the 'Food Quality Control and Management' track spends the second year at Udine, and the Cork track has only 5 places, so the Udine association should not be presented to applicants as the base location. IB/high-school English recognition as C1 is an unusually generous unibz rule worth double-checking case by case with the unibz Language Centre.
